questions.text: Suppose two jobs, each of which needs 10 minutes of CPU time, start simultaneously. Assume 50% I/O wait time. How long will it take for both to complete, if they run sequentially?
questions.solution:
With 50% I/O wait, each job needs 10 min of CPU plus 10 min of I/O = 20 min.

Run one after the other: 20 + 20 = 40 min.

Answer: 40

questions.text: Increasing the RAM of a computer typically improves performance because:
questions.solution:
More RAM holds more pages of running programs, so fewer page faults (slow disk accesses) happen.

Answer: Fewer page faults occur

questions.text:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:
At a particular time of computation, the value of a counting semaphore is 7. Then 20 P operations and 15 V operations were completed on this semaphore. The resulting value of the semaphore is :
questions.solution:
Each P decreases the value by 1 and each V increases it by 1.

7 [latex]-[/latex] 20 + 15 = 2

Answer: 2

questions.text: Suppose a system contains n processes and system uses the round-robin algorithm for CPU scheduling then which data structure is best suited ready queue of the process
questions.solution:
Round robin keeps giving the CPU to the next process and puts the current one back at the end, cycling through all processes. A circular queue models this naturally.

Answer: circular queue
